items.excerpt: Inside Google's Flow Sessions, the residency-style program that hands filmmakers Veo and Flow and screens the results. It doubles as a showcase for how badly Google wants the film industry to build on its generative video stack.

Asteria, the AI studio co-founded by Bryn Mooser and Natasha Lyonne, has struck a strategic partnership with virtual production studio ZeroSpace. The deal pairs Asteria's clean-trained generative models with ZeroSpace's stage, mocap and volumetric capture pipeline.

Higgsfield has inked likeness deals for AI avatars of streamer N3on and UFC fighters Israel Adesanya and Quinton 'Rampage' Jackson. The project is a test for how public figures can get paid to see their likenesses and scripts adapted with generative AI.

Portuguese auteur Edgar Pera discusses 'Asphalt Guerrilla,' premiering at Locarno, which blends fact, fiction and AI-generated imagery into a story about filmmaking. He explains how he uses AI as a craft tool precisely to argue against it.

Locarno Pro's 2026 industry program is built around 'power, people, data,' putting AI, algorithms and consolidation versus creative freedom at the center. Industry strand director Markus Duffner lays out the sessions aimed at working filmmakers.

'Wild at Heart' and 'Twin Peaks' producer Sigurjon Sighvatsson, a Locarno honoree, talks AI, Netflix and the end of the 'mega cinema' era. He argues smaller festivals and human-authored work will outlast the current wave.
The BAFTA TV Awards has added an AI clause to its entry rules, requiring entrants to account for generative AI used in a production. HBO Max shows also become eligible for the first time.

Gregg Araki says he is 'not a big supporter' of AI but found it genuinely useful in the edit on 'I Want Your Sex,' using it to solve a scene he could not otherwise cut. A rare concrete account of AI inside an auteur's post workflow.

MZed's AI Masking course adds lessons on Premiere Pro's native AI object masking and on handling overlapping performances in DaVinci Resolve. The update tracks how fast AI roto and masking are being absorbed into standard NLE workflows.

A UC Riverside-led team has built a tool that goes beyond flagging a video as synthetic: it tries to identify which AI model generated it. For filmmakers and rights holders, that is provenance at the model level.

Wonder Dynamics co-founders Tye Sheridan and Nikola Todorovic explain how their filmmaking backgrounds shaped AI production tools built for artists rather than prompters. They walk through the design decisions behind keeping humans in the loop.

Real actors, real performances, an AI-generated world: Damian Allen walks through Beeble's hybrid film-set workflow shot by shot. It is a concrete preview of a production model where live plates and generative environments are relit together.

Filmmaker Bob Gaudette and producer Kirk Hipkiss have launched Nolia, a Toronto AI-native film and TV company built around original IP. Gaudette's short 'A Face Only a Mother Could Love' won the $50,000 Grand Prix at the 2026 Runway AI Festival.

VFX supervisor Todd Sheridan Perry gives an artist's-eye read on SIGGRAPH 2026, sorting the genuinely useful neural rendering and pipeline tools from the noise. Notably candid about what the shrinking floor means for CG craft.

Curious Refuge's weekly roundup of 16 AI filmmaking updates, covering new model releases, tool changes and festival news filmmakers missed. A fast survey of the week's generative video landscape from a working AI-film school.

A hands-on test of xAI's new AI video tool from a filmmaking perspective, judging shot control, consistency and whether the output survives an edit. Curious Refuge compares it against the current model leaders.
